title: Accurate and bounded approximation of quantum correlation functions
abstract: The exact classical simulation of non-integrable quantum systems rapidly becomes intractable beyond small system sizes, yet its role is central to predicting many-body dynamics. Approximate methods alleviate this cost but typically lack rigorous guarantees on their deviation from the exact result. For the infinite-temperature correlation function, we derive a rigorous error bound for approximating the full dynamics within a computable finite-sized region. Applied to autocorrelations, this finite-region approach is especially accurate across one-dimensional systems and beyond, and can further provide rigorous error bounds for other approximate methods, demonstrated here for matrix-product-operator simulations.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework to bound the error when approximating quantum correlation functions using finite-window methods. By deriving a tight error bound, the authors provide a powerful tool to validate and improve numerical simulations of complex, non-integrable quantum many-body systems in 1D and 2D geometries.
main_problem: The exact simulation of non-integrable quantum systems is computationally intractable, and existing approximate methods lack rigorous guarantees on their error.
main_result: The authors derive a rigorous, computable error bound for approximating quantum correlation functions using finite-window methods, showing this bound is tighter than simpler estimates.
method: The core method involves the window approximation, which decomposes the full system into a finite window and its environment, and then deriving error bounds for correlation functions using techniques involving operator deviations and the Hilbert-Schmidt norm.
model_or_system: The analysis is applied to non-integrable quantum spin systems, specifically using the mixed-field Ising and isotropic Heisenberg models on 1D and 2D lattices.
key_observables: Quantum correlation functions, particularly the infinite-temperature autocorrelation function $C_j(t) = 2^{-n} 	ext{tr}(A_j(t)B)$.
important_parameters: System size (1D, 2D), time $t$, window radius $R$, and simulation parameters like bond dimension ($\chi$) and time step ($dt$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on setting up and solving equations of motion for observable deviations ($\Delta A, \Delta B$) and assumes specific properties like $	ext{tr}([V, A_W]B_W) = 0$ under standard couplings.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the window approximation concept (Fig. 1), compare the true error against derived bounds ($B_O(t)$ vs $B_C(t)$) for 1D systems (Fig. 2), show the accuracy dependence on window size $R$ (Fig. 3), and compare MPO vs. window approximations in 2D (Fig. 5).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the necessity of approximation methods, derives the rigorous error bound $B_C(t)$ for the window approximation, applies this bound to 1D and 2D spin models, and finally compares the resulting error bounds against established MPO simulation results.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial theoretical tool for analyzing non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in complex systems where exact simulation is impossible, offering quantifiable error control for numerical techniques like MPS/MPO.

The local observable X is initially confined to the central site of a finite-window of spins (shown by the blue region) within the larger system. As this observable evolves with the system’s interactions, shown by the black connecting lines, the observable expands to op- erators with support growing from the initial site (shown by the growing orange region). After a finite time, the operator growth reaches the window boundary couplings V , shown in red, where the evolution of X within the window can deviate from the full-system evolution.
